title: Pylint skipping similarly named project directory.
body:
### Bug description

```python
In working on my project, I found that there was a discrepancy between the number of files being checked and how many files I had in my project, which includes both a `applications` and a `applications_api` module. In single stepping through `PyLinter._discover_files()`, I found that it would first walk over `applications`, add it to the `skip_subtrees` list, then when it hit the `applications_api` module, it would falsely skip it as having already been discovered.

Given that both of these are directories which include an `__init__.py` file, the solution is to append the OS directory separator to the name when appending the directory to the `skip_subtrees` list on line 688. I will be following this up with a PR with that fix.

The URL for my project is https://github.com/cinnion/job-application-tracker and I am running tests against the version tagged v1.99.1.
```

### Configuration

```ini
[tool.pylint.main]
django-settings-module="job_application_tracker.settings"
load-plugins = [
    "pylint_django",
    "pylint_per_file_ignores",
]
max-line-length = 120
ignore = [
    ".git",
    ".venv",
    "__pycache__",
    "manage.py",
    "node_modules"
]
jobs = 0
recursive = true
source-roots = "."
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --verbose --recursive=y .

or

pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')
```

### Pylint output

```python
For the command `pylint --verbose --recursive=y .`, the output is as follows (less the fixmes):


(.venv) [cinnion@wing-1 job-application-tracker]$ pylint --verbose --recursive=y .
Using config file /home/cinnion/git.github/job-application-tracker/pyproject.toml

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 9.98/10 (previous run: 9.98/10, +0.00)
Checked 43 files/modules (), skipped 0 files/modules



With the command `pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')`, the output is as follows:


(.venv) [cinnion@wing-1 job-application-tracker]$ pylint --verbose --recursive=y $(git ls-files '*.py')
Using config file /home/cinnion/git.github/job-application-tracker/pyproject.toml

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 9.98/10 (previous run: 9.98/10, +0.00)
Checked 58 files/modules (), skipped 3 files/modules
```

### Expected behavior

I would have expected more than 43 files to have been checked in the first case. In debugging, I tracked down 6 files as being "legitimately" skipped, due to an undocumented behaviour of `pylint-django` adding "migrations" to the ignore list, but that still leaves 9 files being missed, which is directly attributable to it skipping `applications_api` in the walk of the tree in `_discover_files()`. This has been verified after I added my fix for issue #10968 to the code.

### Pylint version

```shell
pylint 4.0.5
astroid 4.0.4
Python 3.13.12 (main, Feb  4 2026, 00:00:00) [GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-11)]
```

RHEL 9.7 and Rocky 9.7

```python
Please see my project at https://github.com/cinnion/job-application-tracker
```

title: E1121 (too-many-function-args) triggered incorrectly when metaclass __call__ accepts more arguments than class __init__
body:
### Bug description


When instantiating a class, pylint strictly checks the arguments against the class's `__init__`. However, if the class uses a metaclass that overrides `__call__` with a different signature, the metaclass's `__call__` signature should dictate the valid arguments, not `__init__`.

This results in pylint incorrectly raising E1121 on valid code.

```python
class Meta(type):
    def __call__(cls, a: int, b: int) -> "MyClass":
        return super().__call__(a)

class MyClass(metaclass=Meta):
    def __init__(self, a: int) -> None:
        self.a = a

MyClass(1, 2)
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint main.py
```

### Pylint output

```python
************* Module main                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
main2.py:12:0: E1121: Too many positional arguments for constructor call (too-many-function-args)
```

### Expected behavior

I'd expect pylint to refer to the metaclass's `__call__` instead of strictly refering to the class's `__init__`.

### Pylint version

```shell

title: False positive: `nested-min-max` drops trailing arguments when suggesting a splat rewrite
body:
### Bug description

`nested-min-max` (W3301), when it suggests flattening a nested `min`/`max` into a splat call, silently **drops every argument positioned after the splatted one**, so the suggested code computes a different result than the original.

```python
LIST = [1, 2, 3]
max(max(LIST), 5, 7)   # suggests `max(*LIST)`     -> drops 5, 7  (evaluates to 3, not 7)
max(4, max(LIST), 7)   # suggests `max(4, *LIST)`  -> drops 7
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --disable=all --enable=nested-min-max a.py
```

### Pylint output

```
a.py:2:0: W3301: Do not use nested call of 'max'; it's possible to do 'max(*LIST)' instead (nested-min-max)
```

### Expected behavior

The suggestion should preserve the trailing arguments, e.g. `max(max(LIST), 5, 7)` -> `max(*LIST, 5, 7)`.

### Root cause

In `pylint/checkers/nested_min_max.py`, the splat rewrite builds the new args with `*fixed_node.args[idx + 1 : idx]`. That slice has `start > stop`, so it is always empty and every argument after the splat position is discarded. It should be `fixed_node.args[idx + 1 :]`.

This is the same class of defect as #11130 / #11131 (the `key=`/`default=` drop), via a different code path — existing fixtures only splat the **last** argument, where the empty slice happens to coincide with the correct one, so the bug is untested.

### Pylint version

```
pylint 4.x (main branch), astroid 4.x
```

title: duplicate-code drops every copy of a block after the first two
body:
### Bug description

When the same block appears in three or more files, `duplicate-code` reports only the first pair. Every further copy is dropped silently.

`a.py`, `b.py` and `c.py` are identical:

```python
def f(a):
    x = a + 1
    y = x * 2
    z = y - 3
    w = z / 4
    return w
```

### Command used

```shell
symilar -d 4 a.py b.py c.py
```

### Pylint output

```
6 similar lines in 2 files
==a.py:[0:6]
==b.py:[0:6]
   ...
TOTAL lines=18 duplicates=6 percent=33.33
```

### Expected behavior

`6 similar lines in 3 files`, listing `c.py` as well, with `duplicates=12`.

The cause is the `break` in `Symilar._compute_sims`. When a new pair shares a chunk with an existing group, the pair is discarded instead of being added to that group. `tests/test_similar.py::test_duplicate_code_raw_strings_all` has this baked in: its docstring says "Test similar lines in 3 similar files", but it asserts `Similar lines in 2 files`.

On real code (`min-similarity-lines=6`, tests and migrations excluded), merging pairs into groups gives the following. No chunk reported today is lost.

| Corpus | Chunk locations reported today | After fix | Groups with 3+ copies |
|---|---|---|---|
| Django 5.1.2 | 254 | 322 | 44 (largest: 10 copies) |
| scikit-learn main | 118 | 135 | 13 |
| httpx 0.28.0 | 24 | 35 | 7 |
| pylint 4.1.3 | 20 | 22 | 2 |

### Pylint version

```shell
main (2fc0591)
```

body:
### Bug description

```python
When plugins are loaded on the command line, the generated config contains the options of those plugins but not `load-plugins` itself, so pylint rejects the file when it is used as it is (see the output below).

Other options passed on the command line are reflected in the output (`--max-line-length=123` gives `max-line-length = 123`, `--good-names=zz` gives `good-names = ["zz"]`), so `load-plugins` is the odd one out. A `load-plugins` set in a config file is written correctly; only `--load-plugins` and `--enable-all-extensions` lose it, because `Run` loads those plugins and removes the options before the configuration is parsed.

With several extensions loaded the file also gets `W0012 unknown-option-value` for messages in `disable` that belong to those extensions. `--generate-rcfile` behaves the same way.

    pass
except (ValueError, Exception):
    pass

$ pylint --load-plugins=pylint.extensions.overlapping_exceptions \
    --disable=all --enable=overlapping-except --score=n -j2 demo.py
```

An extension shipped with pylint is used only to keep this report reproducible; a 10-line custom
plugin behaves the same way, so what matters is the entry point, not the checker itself.

**Pylint output** (main, `1a60ec190`)

```console
# -j1
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)

# -j2
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)
demo.py:3:7: W0714: Overlapping exceptions (Exception is an ancestor class of ValueError) (overlapping-except)
```

With `--score` enabled the rating drops as well (7.50/10 with `-j1`, 5.00/10 with `-j2`).

**Expected behavior**

One message per occurrence and the same score, whatever `--jobs` is.

**Pylint version**

```console
pylint 4.2.0-dev0 (main, 1a60ec190)   # also reproduced on 4.0.6
astroid 4.0.4
Python 3.12.10 (tags/v3.12.10:0cc8128, Apr  8 2025, 12:21:36) [MSC v.1943 64 bit (AMD64)]
```

**OS / Environment**

Windows 11 (`Windows-11-10.0.26100-SP0`). Nothing platform specific: it is a duplicated
registration, not a scheduling issue.

**Additional dependencies**

None.

---

## Additional context: suspected cause

Not a proposed fix, just the result of local investigation.

`_worker_initialize()` deregisters `_registered_dynamic_plugin_checkers` before calling
`load_plugin_modules(..., force=True)`, precisely so that the "old" checker does not survive the
re-registration — that is the fix from #10642. The set is filled in `config_initialization.py` as
`_registered_checkers.difference(default_checkers)`, and `default_checkers` is snapshotted *after*
`Run.__init__` already loaded the `--load-plugins` modules (and after `init-hook` ran). Those
checkers are therefore part of the baseline, never enter the set, and the deregistration is a no-op.

| `--load-plugins` | 1 | **2** |
| `init-hook` | 1 | **2** |
| `load-plugins` in rcfile | 1 | 1 |

The rcfile row is the one #10642 covers. On the 4.0 branch the rcfile path is affected as well,
since that branch predates #10642.

I have a patch for `main` with a regression test and will open a PR referring to this issue.
